article.headline: Unified frameworks for multimodal perception and generation
article.lead: Recent studies introduce innovative frameworks that enhance multimodal perception and generation, achieving significant performance improvements across various tasks. These methods leverage advanced architectures and training techniques to optimize efficiency and accuracy.

paragraphs.text: Lyris presents a long video generation framework that uses a persistent point-cloud memory with a vision-language model. This method generates over three-minute videos with improved spatial consistency, reducing camera error by 3.8x and enhancing return consistency by 22% across four datasets (1). WorldLatent introduces a unified 4D latent space framework that combines world perception and generation, achieving specialist-level zero-shot 4D perception and coherent generation, thus addressing the fragmented nature of traditional models (2). CrownFusion employs a latent diffusion model for generating 3D dental crowns from geometry images, achieving higher spatial resolutions and reducing smoothing artifacts, while also releasing a dataset to support further research (5). ViDiHand2 reformulates video diffusion model depth estimation into geometric constraint solving, achieving a 42% reduction in joint error and improving processing speed (12). The Native Latent Action Models (LAMs) framework extracts dynamics from video data efficiently, achieving a 93.6% success rate on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark (11). The On-Policy Codec Distillation method reduces redundant tokens in video models, achieving a 66% average pruning without quality loss (3). The FlowMap distillation enhancements improve generation quality and reduce drift in autoregressive video models (4).

Hindsight Twins (HinT) distills only the velocity difference between intended fixes and observed errors in text-to-image models, achieving alignment gains that match or exceed previous techniques (6). SPROUT optimizes prompt selection in text-to-image preference tuning, reducing computational waste and achieving comparable performance to uniform sampling (8). The DiLE framework enhances universal multimodal embeddings by integrating task guidance with on-policy retrieval feedback, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks (16).

Déjà VAE detects generated images by analyzing autoencoder traces, achieving a detection accuracy of 94-100% at a 5% false-alarm rate (7). SynthDCB introduces a benchmark for device control evaluation through world distillation, achieving an 88.8% mean Pass@1 across 22 evaluated models (10). Open Vision Banana adapts a diffusion generator into a unified model for various visual perception tasks, revealing performance gaps compared to closed systems (14).

The Beam model features a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 501.3B parameters, optimizing for coding and reasoning tasks while achieving significant efficiency in inference compute (15). UNIFIED integrates encoding, generating, and decoding into a single transformer model, outperforming previous frameworks with fewer parameters (13).

Innata-0 introduces a novel embodied world system that integrates a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture for world-action modeling with a coordinated agent capable of long-horizon execution.
